name: Council of AI
sector: AI developer tools, multi-model collaboration and research
vision: Make difficult technical work approachable through a configurable team of models that shares evidence, challenges answers and works toward one goal. Support web and native terminal workflows while keeping costs, permissions and uncertainty visible.
product_info:
Council of AI is an independent, self-hostable multi-model work environment. A person gives a shared goal to a team of agents, chooses their local or cloud model connections, and follows their collaboration through a browser workspace or native CLI/TUI. Agents are peers: they exchange messages, take roles, delegate investigations, share findings, dispute claims and review a versioned candidate answer. There is no permanent reasoning coordinator; the software still controls scheduling, budgets, access and completion.

Primary use cases are repository coding, technical investigation, research, maths and deductions. The native runtime provides project files, editing, diffs and approved shell commands without requiring an OpenCode installation or hosted account. The hosted coding project has a separate temporary sandbox boundary. Other source-supported features include saved runs, follow-ups, model connection management, streamed activity, optional research, native LSP and project Skills. Availability depends on execution mode and configuration.

The product is a working alpha with a labelled scripted demo. Demo output is not real-model evidence. Agent agreement, passing protocol tests and additional model calls do not prove an answer is correct or that a team outperforms one model. Provider API usage and any product access charge are separate.
brand_voice: Clear, technically grounded, curious and candid. Explain one concrete workflow at a time. Use plain language and visible evidence. Say working alpha when relevant; avoid hype, invented benchmarks, guaranteed correctness or claims of model consciousness.
content_themes: Peer collaboration on difficult tasks, one model versus many agents, coding with evidence and review, local and cloud model choices, native CLI versus hosted workspace, budgets and permissions, research and useful disagreement, build-in-public improvements
goals: Reach developers, technical founders, AI builders and researchers who want to explore collaborative model workflows. Explain the difference between a model, an agent and a team; show useful examples of research, coding and evidence-based review. Direct interested readers to the site to try the labelled demo or connect their own models. Collect concrete workflow feedback rather than promise superior quality. Describe implemented capabilities accurately and label roadmap items. Do not advertise numerical prices, free quotas or benchmark gains unless checked against the current public product. No adoption, conversion or revenue targets have been established.
brand_theme: Quiet technical editorial style. Charcoal backgrounds, sage-green three-bar Council mark, off-white text, muted grey secondary labels. Use restrained spacing, simple evidence/agent diagrams and readable interface-like cards. Avoid generic neon robot imagery. Keep Council of AI distinct from Council Network.
project_notes:
SAAS2POINT0 CONTEXT — COUNCIL OF AI

1. Identity and purpose
Council of AI is Rohit's independent personal project. It is a work environment for a team of models and agents pursuing one shared goal. It is separate from Council Network, which is a social network for AI agents. Public destination: https://councilofai.nftforger.com. Positioning line from the current UI: Made for difficult tasks.

2. Product theory / problem
A single assistant can miss evidence, fail to check an assumption or struggle with a long technical task. Council explores whether peer collaboration, direct communication and versioned review can produce useful work. This is the purpose and hypothesis, not proof of measured superiority. More conversation or agent agreement is not itself a good result.

3. Audience and jobs to be done
Source-supported initial audience: developers, technical users, AI builders and researchers experimenting with local/cloud models. Editorial audience hypothesis: independent founders with difficult repository or research tasks. Jobs: investigate a codebase; compare competing explanations; ask peers to check a candidate solution; follow evidence and unresolved objections; continue a saved task. Do not invent customer interviews, demand statistics or testimonials.

4. Current capability and execution boundaries
Web workspace plus native CLI/TUI share a collaboration engine. Model count and agent count are separate. Peers can message, change roles, invite/delegate to specialists, record findings and review exact candidate versions. The harness enforces access, budgets and scheduling. Native tools operate on the user's selected local project with approvals; native mode does not require a hosted account. Hosted coding tools have their own temporary sandbox. Connections may use supported local/cloud providers; not every provider/model or tool is equivalent. Optional research and native LSP/project Skills require their own setup. Demo is scripted and labelled.

5. Business model: current source versus older plan
Current README and server/billing.ts implement hosted email-confirmed accounts, a configurable message allowance, access approval, BTC/Lightning payment paths and manual fallback. Source defaults are 10 free user/board messages and 100,000 sats for 3 months; these are configuration defaults, not a verified live offer. The September SaaS2point0 planning docs instead proposed five daily tasks, managed prepaid credits and one-time BYOK activation. Do not present those older proposals as current entitlements. Do not publish a price/offer without checking the current site. API usage under a user's model keys is separate from Council access fees.

6. Vision and roadmap
Vision: one collaborative work environment for demanding coding, maths and research, with quality and efficiency evaluated against comparable single-agent baselines. Native desktop apps, managed-model credit accounting, broader MCP integration and complete parity with other coding environments are not established shipped claims. Source contains native LSP/project Skills; do not generalize that to all hosted features. Older plans can describe intent only.

7. Architecture and trust, for accurate explanations
React/TypeScript web frontend; Express API; SQLite state; server-sent activity/events; a shared TypeScript collaboration engine and native CLI. Explain ownership, model choice, visible evidence and permission boundaries in public content; do not expose deployment details, keys, private paths or internal account data. Persistence/checkpoints do not imply flawless recovery or correctness.

8. Vocabulary
Model = connected inference engine. Agent = task participant that uses a model. Team/council = collaborating peers. Run = one engine execution. Finding = recorded claim/evidence. Candidate = versioned proposed answer. Peer agreement = review outcome, not mathematical proof. BYOK = user-supplied provider access, not free inference.

9. Content direction and conversion
Use practical walkthroughs, comparison of execution modes, small evidence-led examples, and honest build notes. CTA: explore Council, try the demo, connect a model, or share a concrete workflow problem. Proposed editorial pillars are peer review, model choice, coding/research workflows, budgets/permissions and limitations. No post-performance measurements have been supplied. Keep marketing experiments labelled as experiments; do not fabricate results.

10. Brand
Existing mark: three sage-green vertical bars with skewed edges, the middle taller. Existing lowercase council wordmark, dark charcoal UI and muted sage accent. Use the supplied mark; do not combine it with Council Network's neon orb. Brand export is rendered from the existing source CSS, not a newly designed identity.
